issues.legal_issue: A will produced after the killings does not discredit an alleged property-related motive where there is no evidence that the accused knew of it at the time.
material_facts: The alleged motive was that one branch of a family sought to obtain the share of agricultural property belonging to another branch, whose members could inherit it.
A will in favour of another person was produced only after the killings in civil proceedings.
There was no evidence that the accused knew of the will when the killings occurred.
issues.conclusion: The will did not undermine the alleged motive, which the Court accepted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the alleged motive against the evidence of what the accused knew when the offence occurred. A will produced subsequently could not displace the motive without evidence that the accused knew of it at the time.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and will_produced_after_offense and no_evidence_accused_knew_of_will and property_based_motive_evidenced

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.will_produced_after_offense: A will relevant to the disputed property was produced after the alleged offence.
predicates.no_evidence_accused_knew_of_will: No evidence showed that the accused knew of the will when the alleged offence occurred.
predicates.property_based_motive_evidenced: Evidence showed a dispute or interest concerning property that could provide a motive for the offence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a property-based motive, a will produced after the offence without evidence of the accused's prior knowledge does not defeat that motive.

issues.legal_issue: Eyewitness testimony may be accepted despite the non-examination of independent witnesses when the available witnesses were examined and their accounts are corroborated.
material_facts: Three eyewitnesses testified about the killings.
The nearby area was sparsely inhabited, and no other person was shown to have been available at the time.
The witnesses' names appeared in a report lodged immediately after the incident.
Their testimony was corroborated by medical evidence, and the lower courts accepted it.
issues.conclusion: The Court found the eyewitness testimony reliable and held that the failure to examine independent witnesses did not undermine it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the eyewitness accounts in light of their prompt identification in the First Information Report, medical corroboration, and the circumstances explaining why other independent witnesses were not examined. It found no basis to reject the accounts.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and eyewitnesses_examined and eyewitness_accounts_promptly_reported and medical_evidence_corrobates_accounts and no_other_available_witness_shown

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.eyewitnesses_examined: People who witnessed the incident testified at trial.
predicates.eyewitness_accounts_promptly_reported: The eyewitnesses were identified in a report made soon after the incident.
predicates.medical_evidence_corrobates_accounts: Medical evidence was consistent with the eyewitness accounts.
predicates.no_other_available_witness_shown: The evidence did not show that other independent witnesses were available to be examined.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, eyewitness testimony is accepted where the witnesses testified, their accounts were promptly reported and medically corroborated, and no other available witnesses were shown.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the recorded timing of a First Information Report is not established where it was not tested in cross-examination and the evidence does not show that the timing was impossible.
material_facts: The report recorded that the incident occurred at about 7:30 p.m. and was lodged at 8:30 p.m.
The police station was stated to be 12.5 kilometres from the scene.
No witness was asked in cross-examination whether the time of the incident had been accurately noted.
The evidence did not establish how the informants travelled or show that the reported timing was impossible.
The report described the incident and corroborated the eyewitnesses.
issues.conclusion: In the absence of material undermining the timing, the Court treated the report as having been recorded immediately after the incident and rejected the challenge.
issues.legal_principle: In considering the timing of a First Information Report under Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Court held that a claim that the stated times were incompatible should be tested by questions in cross-examination and supported by evidence. Without such material, the prompt report and its corroborative account stood.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and fir_timing_challenged and timing_challenge_not_put_in_cross_examination and no_evidence_report_timing_impossible and report_corrobates_eyewitnesses

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.fir_timing_challenged: A party disputed whether the recorded times of the incident and report were credible.
predicates.timing_challenge_not_put_in_cross_examin: No witness or informant was questioned in cross-examination about whether the incident time had been accurately recorded.
predicates.no_evidence_report_timing_impossible: The evidence did not establish circumstances making the recorded report time impossible.
predicates.report_corrobates_eyewitnesses: The report's description of the incident supported the eyewitness accounts.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, a timing challenge to a corroborative report is rejected as unsupported when it was not tested in cross-examination and evidence does not show that the timing was impossible.

issues.legal_issue: A prior complaint against police officers does not establish police bias in a murder investigation without evidence connecting the investigating officers to the complaint or showing actual prejudice.
material_facts: One accused had earlier made an application containing allegations against police officers.
The application did not refer to the officers in charge of the murder investigation.
The report of the incident was lodged promptly and described the accused's alleged roles.
There was no evidence that the investigating officer was prejudiced against the accused.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the claim that police bias had led to the accused's false implication.
issues.legal_principle: A prior complaint against some police officers does not, by itself, establish that officers investigating a later case were biased or falsely implicated an accused. The Court required material indicating actual prejudice or a connection to the investigation.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and prior_complaint_against_police and complaint_unconnected_to_investigators and no_evidence_investigator_prejudice

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.prior_complaint_against_police: The accused had previously made a complaint or application against police officers.
predicates.complaint_unconnected_to_investigators: The prior complaint did not identify the officers conducting the investigation in the present case.
predicates.no_evidence_investigator_prejudice: No evidence showed that the investigating officer was prejudiced against the accused.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, a prior complaint against police does not establish investigative bias when it is unconnected to the investigators and there is no evidence of their prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence may be maintained for an offender whose property-driven attack involved brutal and determined killings.
material_facts: The offender and his father were interested in obtaining property that could be claimed by the deceased family.
The offender killed two members of that family, including a close relative and a young woman.
He chopped the man's neck and inflicted repeated blows on the young woman.
The offender's death sentences had been confirmed on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Court saw no reason to alter the death sentence imposed on this offender.
issues.legal_principle: In considering whether death was justified, the Court referred to Dalbir Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab, [1979] 3 SCR 1059, concerning reasons that may weigh in favour of a death sentence. It relied on the offender's property-related motive and the brutal, determined manner in which he killed two victims. The convictions arose under Sections 302 and 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

predicates.appeal_against_death_sentence: The case is an appeal challenging a death sentence.
predicates.offender_had_property_based_motive: The offender acted in pursuit of a motive to obtain property or defeat another person's claim to it.
predicates.offender_committed_brutal_determined_kil: The offender personally carried out killings in a brutal and determined manner.

issues.definition: A death sentence is maintained on appeal where the offender acted from a property-based motive and personally committed brutal, determined killings.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence is not justified for a participant who had no motive of his own and was drawn into the killings, even where his injuries were cruelly inflicted.
material_facts: The offender was not connected to the family or its property dispute.
He inflicted three blows on one victim with a weapon he carried.
The Court found that he had no motive of his own and appeared to have been drawn into the killings.
He had been convicted for the murder in conjunction with the other participants.
issues.conclusion: The Court maintained the conviction but altered this offender's death sentence to imprisonment for life.
issues.legal_principle: In considering sentence under Sections 302 and 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, the Court distinguished a participant who had no motive and appeared to have been drawn into the killing from the offender who pursued the property motive and committed the other brutal killings. It held the death sentence unjustified in the former circumstances.

rule.if: appeal_against_death_sentence and offender_participated_in_killing and offender_had_no_personal_motive and offender_was_drawn_into_killing

predicates.appeal_against_death_sentence: The case is an appeal challenging a death sentence.
predicates.offender_participated_in_killing: The offender took part in the killing, including by inflicting injuries on a victim.
predicates.offender_had_no_personal_motive: The offender had no personal motive for the killing.
predicates.offender_was_drawn_into_killing: The circumstances indicated that the offender was drawn into the killing rather than acting to pursue his own motive.

issues.definition: On appeal, a participant's death sentence is replaced with life imprisonment where he took part in a killing but had no personal motive and was drawn into it.
